# =============================================================================
# Harmonia Beaker LLM Agent Environment - Apptainer Definition
# =============================================================================
# This definition builds an Apptainer image with:
# - Beaker kernel for interactive notebooks
# - BDI-Kit context for data harmonization
# - any-llm-sdk for unified LLM provider access (30+ providers)
# - Full support for anyllm:ollama, anyllm:openai, etc.
#
# Build with:
#   ./build_harmonia_apptainer.sh
#
# Or manually:
#   srun -J apptainer_build_claude-code --time=02:00:00 --mem=32G --gres=tmpspace:100G bash -c "
#     cd /hpc/compgen/projects/llm_GEO_project/harmonia_metadata_agent/analysis/dstoker/harmonia
#     export TMPDIR=\$TMPDIR APPTAINER_TMPDIR=\$TMPDIR APPTAINER_CACHEDIR=\$TMPDIR
#     apptainer build harmonia_beaker_LLM_agent_environment_apptainer.sif harmonia_beaker_LLM_agent_environment_apptainer.def
#   "
# =============================================================================

Bootstrap: docker
From: python:3.11

%post
    # ==========================================================================
    # Phase 1: Environment Setup
    # ==========================================================================
    # Use /var/tmp for builds - it has more space than /tmp in container
    export TMPDIR=/var/tmp
    export UV_CACHE_DIR=/var/tmp/uv_cache
    export PIP_CACHE_DIR=/var/tmp/pip_cache
    mkdir -p /var/tmp/uv_cache /var/tmp/pip_cache

    echo "=== Initial space ==="
    df -h /var/tmp /tmp

    # Create jupyter user
    useradd -m jupyter

    # Install system dependencies
    apt update && apt install -y lsof git curl

    # ==========================================================================
    # Phase 2: Python Package Management Setup
    # ==========================================================================
    # Install uv for fast package management
    pip install --no-cache-dir uv

    # Install hatch and hatchling for building packages
    TMPDIR=/var/tmp uv pip install --system --no-cache hatch hatchling

    echo "=== Space after hatch install ==="
    df -h /var/tmp

%files
    # Copy only essential files, NOT .sif containers
    src /jupyter/src
    pyproject.toml /jupyter/pyproject.toml
    README.md /jupyter/README.md
    # Note: dou.csv is accessed via bind mount at runtime, not copied into image

%post
    # ==========================================================================
    # Phase 3: Main Package Installation
    # ==========================================================================
    # Use /var/tmp for builds - it has more space than /tmp in container
    export TMPDIR=/var/tmp
    export UV_CACHE_DIR=/var/tmp/uv_cache
    export PIP_CACHE_DIR=/var/tmp/pip_cache
    mkdir -p /var/tmp/uv_cache /var/tmp/pip_cache

    chown -R 1000:1000 /jupyter

    # Safety: Remove any accidentally copied .sif files
    echo "=== Cleaning up any .sif files ==="
    find /jupyter -name "*.sif*" -type f -delete 2>/dev/null || true

    echo "=== Space before main install ==="
    df -h /var/tmp

    # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Install beaker_kernel (provides hatch build hook and kernel functionality)
    # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    echo "Installing beaker_kernel (provides hatch build hook)..."
    TMPDIR=/var/tmp uv pip install --system --no-cache "beaker_kernel>=1.14.0"

    # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Install any-llm-sdk with provider dependencies
    # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # any-llm-sdk provides unified access to 30+ LLM providers
    # We install with ollama extra for local LLM support
    echo "Installing any-llm-sdk with ollama provider..."
    TMPDIR=/var/tmp uv pip install --system --no-cache "any-llm-sdk[ollama] @ git+https://github.com/mozilla-ai/any-llm.git"

    # Verify any-llm installation
    echo "=== Verifying any-llm installation ==="
    python3 -c "from any_llm import AnyLLM; print('any_llm imported successfully')"
    python3 -c "import ollama; print('ollama package imported successfully')"

    # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Install additional dependencies for archytas
    # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # These are needed for message conversion and tool handling
    echo "Installing langchain-core for message types..."
    TMPDIR=/var/tmp uv pip install --system --no-cache langchain-core

    # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Build and install bdikit_context
    # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    cd /jupyter
    echo "Building and installing bdikit_context (with --no-build-isolation to use system packages)..."
    TMPDIR=/var/tmp pip install --no-cache-dir --no-build-isolation .

    # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Verify installations
    # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    echo "=== Verifying bdikit_context installation ==="
    python3 -c "from bdikit_context.context import BDIKitContext; print('BDIKitContext imported successfully')"
    python3 -c "from bdikit_context.agent import BDIKitAgent; print('BDIKitAgent imported successfully')"

    echo "=== Verifying code_context installation ==="
    python3 -c "from code_context.context import CodeContext; print('CodeContext imported successfully')"

    echo "=== Verifying bdikit_context.llm.anyllm installation ==="
    python3 -c "from bdikit_context.llm.anyllm import AnyLLMModel; print('AnyLLMModel imported successfully')"
    python3 -c "from bdikit_context.llm.anyllm import ChatAnyLLM; print('ChatAnyLLM imported successfully')"

    # Verify entry points are registered
    echo "=== Verifying entry points ==="
    python3 -c "from importlib.metadata import entry_points; contexts = [ep.name for ep in entry_points(group='beaker.contexts')]; print(f'Registered contexts: {contexts}')"

    # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Create legacy JSON mapping file as fallback
    # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
    echo "Creating legacy context mapping file..."
    mkdir -p /usr/local/share/beaker/contexts
    cat > /usr/local/share/beaker/contexts/bdikit_context.json << 'EOF'
{
    "slug": "bdikit_context",
    "package": "bdikit_context.context",
    "class_name": "BDIKitContext"
}
EOF
    echo "Created /usr/local/share/beaker/contexts/bdikit_context.json"
    cat /usr/local/share/beaker/contexts/bdikit_context.json

    cat > /usr/local/share/beaker/contexts/code_context.json << 'EOF'
{
    "slug": "code_context",
    "package": "code_context.context",
    "class_name": "CodeContext"
}
EOF
    echo "Created /usr/local/share/beaker/contexts/code_context.json"
    cat /usr/local/share/beaker/contexts/code_context.json

    # ==========================================================================
    # Phase 4: Cleanup
    # ==========================================================================
    echo "=== Cleaning up temp files ==="
    rm -rf /var/tmp/uv_cache /var/tmp/pip_cache

    echo "=== Space after main install ==="
    df -h /var/tmp

    echo "=== Final /jupyter contents ==="
    ls -la /jupyter/

    echo "=== Installed packages (key ones) ==="
    python3 -c "import pkg_resources; pkgs = ['beaker-kernel', 'any-llm-sdk', 'bdikit-context', 'langchain-core', 'ollama']; [print(f'{p}: {pkg_resources.get_distribution(p).version}') for p in pkgs if any(d.key == p for d in pkg_resources.working_set)]" 2>/dev/null || true

    echo ""
    echo "=============================================="
    echo "BUILD COMPLETE"
    echo "=============================================="

%environment
    export PYTHONPATH=/jupyter
    # Ensure SSL certificates are available for API calls
    export SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
    export REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt

%runscript
    cd /jupyter
    exec beaker dev watch --ip 0.0.0.0

%labels
    Author dstoker
    Version 1.0
    Description Harmonia Beaker LLM Agent Environment with any-llm-sdk support

%help
    Harmonia Beaker LLM Agent Environment
    =====================================

    This container provides:
    - Beaker kernel for interactive notebooks
    - BDI-Kit context for data harmonization to GDC schema
    - any-llm-sdk for unified LLM provider access

    Supported LLM providers via anyllm:
    - Local: ollama, lmstudio, vllm, llamafile
    - Cloud: openai, anthropic, mistral, groq, together, perplexity, deepseek
    - Gateway: openrouter, azure, bedrock, vertexai

    Usage:
        # Start Beaker server
        ./exec_apptainer_harmonia.sh --config configs/manual/my_config.yaml

        # Or manually
        apptainer exec --bind .:/jupyter harmonia_beaker_LLM_agent_environment_apptainer.sif \
            beaker dev watch --ip 0.0.0.0 --port 8100

   313→# Function to start Ollama server
   314→start_ollama_server() {
   315→    # Generate log file name based on job name or timestamp
   316→    if [ -n "$JOB_NAME" ]; then
   317→        # Use job name for consistent naming with experiment logs
   318→        OLLAMA_LOG_FILE="${LOGS_DIR}/${JOB_NAME}_ollama.log"
   319→    else
   320→        # Fallback to timestamp if no job name provided
   321→        TIMESTAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)
   322→        OLLAMA_LOG_FILE="${LOGS_DIR}/ollama_${TIMESTAMP}.log"
   323→    fi
   324→
   325→    echo ""
   326→    echo "🦙 Local LLM detected (provider: $LLM_PROVIDER)"
   327→    echo "   Ollama port: ${OLLAMA_PORT}"
   328→
   329→    # --- Per-job isolation setup (SLURM batch mode) ---
   330→    if [ -n "$SLURM_JOB_ID" ]; then
   331→        echo "   SLURM job detected (ID: $SLURM_JOB_ID) - using per-job Ollama isolation"
   332→
   333→        # Per-job PID file
   334→        OLLAMA_PID_FILE="${OLLAMA_DIR}/.ollama_${SLURM_JOB_ID}.pid"
   335→        export OLLAMA_PID_FILE
   336→
   337→        # Per-job OLLAMA_HOME for runtime data isolation
   338→        if [ -n "$TMPDIR" ]; then
   339→            export OLLAMA_HOME="$TMPDIR/ollama_${SLURM_JOB_ID}"
   340→        else
   341→            export OLLAMA_HOME="${OLLAMA_DIR}/ollama_home_${SLURM_JOB_ID}"
   342→        fi
   343→        mkdir -p "$OLLAMA_HOME"
   344→        echo "   OLLAMA_HOME: ${OLLAMA_HOME}"
   345→        echo "   OLLAMA_PID_FILE: ${OLLAMA_PID_FILE}"
   346→
   347→        # Set OLLAMA_HOST for this job's unique port
   348→        export OLLAMA_HOST="0.0.0.0:${OLLAMA_PORT}"
   349→
   350→    else
   351→        echo "   Interactive mode - checking if Ollama server is running on this node ($(hostname))..."
   352→
   353→        # --- Interactive/manual mode: keep original sharing logic ---
   354→        OLLAMA_PROCESS_RUNNING=false
   355→        if pgrep -f "ollama serve" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
   356→            OLLAMA_PROCESS_RUNNING=true
   357→        fi
   358→
   359→        if [ "$OLLAMA_PROCESS_RUNNING" = true ] && curl -s "http://localhost:${OLLAMA_PORT}/api/tags" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
   360→            echo "   ✓ Ollama server already running on port ${OLLAMA_PORT} (this node)"
   361→
   362→            # Check if the required model is available in this Ollama instance
   363→            if ! curl -s "http://localhost:${OLLAMA_PORT}/api/tags" | grep -q "\"name\":\"${LLM_MODEL}\""; then
   364→                echo "   ⚠ Model '${LLM_MODEL}' not found in running Ollama instance"
   365→                echo "     Stopping existing Ollama and starting fresh with model preload..."
   366→                pkill -f "ollama serve" 2>/dev/null || true
   367→                sleep 2
   368→                OLLAMA_PROCESS_RUNNING=false
   369→            else
   370→                echo "   ✓ Model '${LLM_MODEL}' is available"
   371→                if [ -n "$JOB_NAME" ]; then
   372→                    OLLAMA_LOG_FILE="${LOGS_DIR}/${JOB_NAME}_ollama_shared.log"
   373→                else
   374→                    OLLAMA_LOG_FILE="${LOGS_DIR}/ollama_shared_${TIMESTAMP}.log"
   375→                fi
   376→                echo "   Ollama log: ${OLLAMA_LOG_FILE}"
   377→                echo "[$(date)] Ollama server already running on $(hostname) with model ${LLM_MODEL}" > "${OLLAMA_LOG_FILE}"
   378→
   379→                export LLM_BASE_URL="http://$(hostname):${OLLAMA_PORT}"
   380→                export OLLAMA_HOST="http://$(hostname):${OLLAMA_PORT}"
   381→                echo "   LLM_BASE_URL: ${LLM_BASE_URL}"
   382→                echo "   OLLAMA_HOST:  ${OLLAMA_HOST}"
   383→
   384→                return 0
   385→            fi
   386→        fi
   387→
   388→        # If API responds but no local process, it might be from another node - ignore it
   389→        if curl -s "http://localhost:${OLLAMA_PORT}/api/tags" > /dev/null 2>&1 && [ "$OLLAMA_PROCESS_RUNNING" = false ]; then
   390→            echo "   ⚠ Ollama API responds but no local process found"
   391→            echo "     (May be from another HPC node - starting fresh instance)"
   392→        fi
   393→    fi
   394→
   395→    # Check if the Ollama start script exists
   396→    if [ ! -f "${OLLAMA_DIR}/start_ollama.sh" ]; then
   397→        echo "   ERROR: Ollama start script not found at ${OLLAMA_DIR}/start_ollama.sh"

   403→        return 1
   404→    fi
   405→
   406→    echo "   Starting Ollama server..."
   407→    echo "   Ollama log: ${OLLAMA_LOG_FILE}"
   408→
   409→    # Determine per-job serve log name
   410→    OLLAMA_SERVE_LOG="${OLLAMA_DIR}/ollama_serve_${SLURM_JOB_ID:-default}.log"
   411→
   412→    # Start Ollama with logging - capture stdout and stderr
   413→    {
   414→        echo "=============================================="
   415→        echo "Ollama Server Log"
   416→        echo "=============================================="
   417→        echo "Started: $(date)"
   418→        echo "Provider: ${LLM_PROVIDER}"
   419→        echo "Model: ${LLM_MODEL}"
   420→        echo "Port: ${OLLAMA_PORT}"
   421→        echo "Host: $(hostname)"
   422→        if [ -n "$SLURM_JOB_ID" ]; then
   423→            echo "SLURM Job ID: ${SLURM_JOB_ID}"
   424→            echo "OLLAMA_HOME: ${OLLAMA_HOME}"

   426→        fi
   427→        echo "=============================================="
   428→        echo ""
   429→    } > "${OLLAMA_LOG_FILE}"
   430→
   431→    # Export OLLAMA_SERVE_LOG so start_ollama.sh can use it
   432→    export OLLAMA_SERVE_LOG
   433→
   434→    # Start Ollama in background with output redirected to log
   435→    "${OLLAMA_DIR}/start_ollama.sh" >> "${OLLAMA_LOG_FILE}" 2>&1 &
   436→    OLLAMA_START_PID=$!
   437→
   438→    # Wait for the start script to complete
   439→    wait $OLLAMA_START_PID 2>/dev/null || true
   440→
   441→    # Wait for Ollama to be ready (up to 60 seconds)
   442→    echo "   Waiting for Ollama to be ready..."
   443→    OLLAMA_READY=0
   444→    for i in {1..60}; do
   445→        if curl -s "http://localhost:${OLLAMA_PORT}/api/tags" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
   446→            OLLAMA_READY=1
   447→            echo "   ✓ Ollama server is ready (waited ${i}s)"

   452→    done
   453→
   454→    if [ $OLLAMA_READY -eq 0 ]; then

   457→        echo "[$(date)] ERROR: Ollama server failed to start within 60 seconds" >> "${OLLAMA_LOG_FILE}"
   458→        return 1
   459→    fi
   460→
   461→    OLLAMA_STARTED_BY_US=true
   462→
   463→    # Set environment variables for the container
   464→    export LLM_BASE_URL="http://$(hostname):${OLLAMA_PORT}"
   465→    export OLLAMA_HOST="http://$(hostname):${OLLAMA_PORT}"
   466→
   467→    echo "   LLM_BASE_URL: ${LLM_BASE_URL}"
   468→    echo "   OLLAMA_HOST:  ${OLLAMA_HOST}"
   469→    echo ""
   470→
   471→    # Log endpoint info
   472→    {
   473→        echo ""
   474→        echo "[$(date)] Endpoints configured:"
   475→        echo "  LLM_BASE_URL: ${LLM_BASE_URL}"
   476→        echo "  OLLAMA_HOST:  ${OLLAMA_HOST}"
   477→        echo ""
   478→    } >> "${OLLAMA_LOG_FILE}"
   479→
   480→    # Show available models
   481→    echo "   Available Ollama models:"
   482→    curl -s "http://localhost:${OLLAMA_PORT}/api/tags" | python3 -c "
   483→import sys, json
   484→try:
   485→    data = json.load(sys.stdin)
   486→    models = data.get('models', [])
   487→    if models:
   488→        for m in models:
   489→            print(f\"     - {m.get('name', 'unknown')}\")

   491→        print('     (no models installed)')
   492→except:
   493→    print('     (could not list models)')
   494→" 2>/dev/null || echo "     (could not list models)"
   495→    echo ""
   496→
   497→    # Log available models
   498→    {
   499→        echo "[$(date)] Available models:"
   500→        curl -s "http://localhost:${OLLAMA_PORT}/api/tags" 2>/dev/null || echo "  (could not retrieve)"
   501→        echo ""
   502→    } >> "${OLLAMA_LOG_FILE}"
   503→
   504→    # Pre-warm the model if specified (blocking - wait for model to load)
   505→    if [ -n "$LLM_MODEL" ]; then
   506→        echo "   Pre-loading model: ${LLM_MODEL}..."
   507→        echo "[$(date)] Pre-loading model: ${LLM_MODEL}" >> "${OLLAMA_LOG_FILE}"
   508→
   509→        # Build generate request with optional num_ctx for context length
   510→        if [ -n "$OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH" ]; then
   511→            GENERATE_DATA="{\"model\": \"${LLM_MODEL}\", \"prompt\": \"Hello\", \"stream\": false, \"options\": {\"num_ctx\": ${OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH}}}"
   512→            echo "   Context length: ${OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH}"
   513→            echo "[$(date)] Using num_ctx: ${OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH}" >> "${OLLAMA_LOG_FILE}"
   514→        else
   515→            GENERATE_DATA="{\"model\": \"${LLM_MODEL}\", \"prompt\": \"Hello\", \"stream\": false}"
   516→        fi
   517→
   518→        # This call blocks until the model is loaded into memory
   519→        if curl -s "http://localhost:${OLLAMA_PORT}/api/generate" \
   520→            -d "$GENERATE_DATA" \
   521→            >> "${OLLAMA_LOG_FILE}" 2>&1; then
   522→            echo "   ✓ Model preloaded successfully"
   523→            echo "[$(date)] Model preloaded successfully" >> "${OLLAMA_LOG_FILE}"
   524→        else
   525→            echo "   Warning: Model pre-load may have failed"
   526→            echo "[$(date)] Warning: Model pre-load may have failed" >> "${OLLAMA_LOG_FILE}"
   527→        fi
   528→
   529→        # Verify model loading with ollama ps
   530→        echo ""
   531→        echo "   Verifying model status (ollama ps):"
   532→        OLLAMA_PS_OUTPUT=$(OLLAMA_HOST="http://localhost:${OLLAMA_PORT}" "${OLLAMA_DIR}/ollama" ps 2>/dev/null || echo "   (could not run ollama ps)")
   533→        echo "$OLLAMA_PS_OUTPUT" | while IFS= read -r line; do
   534→            echo "     $line"
   535→        done
   536→        echo "[$(date)] ollama ps output:" >> "${OLLAMA_LOG_FILE}"
   537→        echo "$OLLAMA_PS_OUTPUT" >> "${OLLAMA_LOG_FILE}"
   538→
   539→        # Check GPU offload percentage (look at data lines, not header)
   540→        GPU_PCT=$(echo "$OLLAMA_PS_OUTPUT" | grep -oP '\d+%' | head -1)
   541→        if [ -n "$GPU_PCT" ]; then
   542→            if [ "$GPU_PCT" = "0%" ]; then
   543→                echo "   ⚠ WARNING: Model has 0% GPU offload - running on CPU only"
   544→                echo "[$(date)] WARNING: Model has 0% GPU offload" >> "${OLLAMA_LOG_FILE}"
   545→            elif [ "$GPU_PCT" != "100%" ]; then

   547→                echo "[$(date)] WARNING: Model GPU offload is ${GPU_PCT}" >> "${OLLAMA_LOG_FILE}"
   548→            else
   549→                echo "   ✓ Model is 100% GPU offloaded"
   550→            fi
   551→        fi
   552→    fi
   553→
   554→    # Start background process to tail ollama serve log to our log file
   555→    if [ -f "${OLLAMA_SERVE_LOG}" ]; then
   556→        {
   557→            echo ""
   558→            echo "=============================================="
   559→            echo "Ollama Server Output (from ${OLLAMA_SERVE_LOG})"
   560→            echo "=============================================="
   561→        } >> "${OLLAMA_LOG_FILE}"
   562→        # Tail the per-job ollama_serve log in background
   563→        tail -f "${OLLAMA_SERVE_LOG}" >> "${OLLAMA_LOG_FILE}" 2>&1 &
   564→        OLLAMA_TAIL_PID=$!
   565→    fi
   566→
   567→    return 0
   568→}

   570→# Function to stop Ollama server (if we started it)
   571→stop_ollama_server() {
   572→    # Kill the tail process if running
   573→    if [ -n "$OLLAMA_TAIL_PID" ]; then
   574→        kill $OLLAMA_TAIL_PID 2>/dev/null || true
   575→    fi
   576→
   577→    if [ "$OLLAMA_STARTED_BY_US" = true ]; then

   579→        echo "🦙 Stopping Ollama server (port ${OLLAMA_PORT})..."

   581→            echo "[$(date)] Stopping Ollama server (port ${OLLAMA_PORT})..." >> "${OLLAMA_LOG_FILE}"
   582→        fi
   583→
   584→        if [ -n "$SLURM_JOB_ID" ] && [ -n "$OLLAMA_PID_FILE" ] && [ -f "$OLLAMA_PID_FILE" ]; then
   585→            # Per-job cleanup: kill our specific process only
   586→            local pid=$(cat "$OLLAMA_PID_FILE")
   587→            echo "   Killing Ollama PID $pid (job-specific)..."
   588→            kill $pid 2>/dev/null || true

   591→            rm -f "$OLLAMA_PID_FILE"

   594→        else
   595→            # Interactive mode: use shared stop script
   596→            if [ -f "${OLLAMA_DIR}/stop_ollama.sh" ]; then
   597→                "${OLLAMA_DIR}/stop_ollama.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
   598→            fi
   599→        fi
   600→
   601→        if [ -n "$OLLAMA_LOG_FILE" ]; then
   602→            echo "[$(date)] Ollama server stopped." >> "${OLLAMA_LOG_FILE}"
   603→        fi
   604→        echo "   Done."
   605→    fi

    13→BDIKIT_MODELS_CACHE_DIR = os.path.join(BDIKIT_CACHE_DIR, "models")

    25→def download_file_url(url: str, destination: str):
    26→    # start the download stream
    27→    response = requests.get(url, stream=True)
    28→    # read total sizes in bytes from http headers
    29→    total_size = int(response.headers.get("content-length", 0))
    30→    # download the file in chunks and write to destination file
    31→    block_size = 1024
    32→    with tqdm(total=total_size, unit="B", unit_scale=True) as progress_bar:
    33→        with open(destination, "wb") as file:
    34→            for data in response.iter_content(block_size):
    35→                progress_bar.update(len(data))
    36→                file.write(data)
    37→    # check if filed was downloaded completely
    38→    if total_size != 0 and progress_bar.n != total_size:
    39→        raise RuntimeError(

     3→Generate .env files from experiment configuration YAML files.
     4→
     5→This script reads an experiment config and creates an associated .env file
     6→with the appropriate LLM settings, based on the base .env file.
     7→
     8→Usage:
     9→    python generate_env.py --config path/to/config.yaml
    10→    python generate_env.py --config-dir path/to/configs/  # Generate for all configs in directory
    11→"""
    12→
    13→import argparse
    14→import os
    15→import re
    16→import sys
    17→from pathlib import Path
    18→
    19→import yaml
    20→

    22→def load_base_env(base_env_path: Path) -> str:
    23→    """Load the base .env file content."""
    24→    if not base_env_path.exists():
    25→        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Base .env file not found: {base_env_path}")
    26→    return base_env_path.read_text()

    28→
    29→def load_experiment_config(config_path: Path) -> dict:
    30→    """Load experiment configuration from YAML."""
    31→    with open(config_path) as f:
    32→        return yaml.safe_load(f)
    33→
    34→
    35→def update_env_value(env_content: str, key: str, value: str) -> str:
    36→    """Update or add an environment variable in .env content."""
    37→    # Pattern to match the key (with optional comment prefix)
    38→    pattern = rf'^(#\s*)?{re.escape(key)}=.*$'
    39→    replacement = f'{key}={value}'
    40→
    41→    # Check if key exists (commented or not)
    42→    if re.search(pattern, env_content, re.MULTILINE):
    43→        return re.sub(pattern, replacement, env_content, flags=re.MULTILINE)
    44→    else:

    62→        'anyllm:openai': 'bdikit_context.llm.anyllm.AnyLLMModel',

    65→        'anyllm:gemini': 'bdikit_context.llm.anyllm.AnyLLMModel',

    70→def get_api_key_for_provider(provider: str, env_content: str) -> str:
    71→    """Extract the appropriate API key from env content based on provider."""
    72→    # Determine which API key to use based on provider
    73→    if 'openrouter' in provider.lower():

    75→    elif 'openai' in provider.lower():
    76→        match = re.search(r'^OPENAI_API_KEY=(.+)$', env_content, re.MULTILINE)
    77→    elif 'anthropic' in provider.lower():
    78→        match = re.search(r'^ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=(.+)$', env_content, re.MULTILINE)
    79→    elif 'groq' in provider.lower():
    80→        match = re.search(r'^GROQ_API_KEY=(.+)$', env_content, re.MULTILINE)
    81→    elif 'gemini' in provider.lower() or 'google' in provider.lower():
    82→        match = re.search(r'^GOOGLE_API_KEY=(.+)$', env_content, re.MULTILINE)
    83→    elif 'ollama' in provider.lower():
    84→        # Ollama doesn't need an API key

   121→    # Set the import path based on provider

   130→    # Handle base_url and context_length for Ollama

1→import warnings

     3→from litellm import completion
     4→from bdikit.schema_matching.base import BaseTopkSchemaMatcher, ColumnMatch
     5→
     6→
     7→class LLM(BaseTopkSchemaMatcher):
     8→    """A schema matcher that uses LLM to match columns based on their similarity."""
     9→
    10→    def __init__(self, model_name="openai/gpt-4o-mini", **model_kwargs):
    11→        self.model_name = model_name
    12→        self.model_kwargs = model_kwargs
    13→        self.llm_attempts = 5
    14→
    15→    def _sample_values(self, column, max_samples=5):
    16→        values = column.drop_duplicates().dropna()
    17→        if len(values) > max_samples:
    18→            return values.sample(max_samples).tolist()
    19→        else:
    20→            return values.tolist()
    21→
    22→    def rank_schema_matches(self, source, target, top_k):
    23→        matches = []
    24→
    25→        target_cols = [
    26→            "Column: "
    27→            + target_col
    28→            + ", Sample values: ["
    29→            + ",".join(self._sample_values(target[target_col]))
    30→            + "]"
    31→            for target_col in target.columns
    32→        ]
    33→
    34→        for source_col in source.columns:
    35→            cand = (
    36→                "Column: "
    37→                + source_col
    38→                + ", Sample values: ["
    39→                + ",".join(self._sample_values(source[source_col]))
    40→                + "]"
    41→            )
    42→
    43→            targets = "\n".join(target_cols)
    44→
    45→            attempts = 0
    46→            while True:
    47→                if attempts >= self.llm_attempts:
    48→                    warnings.warn(
    49→                        f"Failed to parse response after {self.llm_attempts} attempts. Skipping.",
    50→                        UserWarning,
    51→                    )
    52→                    refined_match = []
    53→                    break
    54→
    55→                refined_match = self._get_matches(cand, targets)
    56→                refined_match = self._parse_matches(refined_match)
    57→                attempts += 1
    58→
    59→                if refined_match is not None:
    60→                    break
    61→
    62→            sorted_matches = sorted(refined_match, key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    63→            for target_col, score in sorted_matches[:top_k]:
    64→                matches.append(ColumnMatch(source_col, target_col, score))
    65→
    66→        matches = self._sort_ranked_matches(matches)
    67→

    77→            "Target Schemas:\n"
    78→            "Column: WorkerID, Sample values: [100, 101, 102]\n"
    79→            "Column: EmpCode, Sample values: [001, 002, 003]\n"
    80→            "Column: StaffName, Sample values: ['Alice', 'Bob', 'Charlie']\n"

    96→            },

    98→                "role": "user",
    99→                "content": prompt,
   100→            },

1→import pandas as pd
     2→from typing import Dict, Any, List
     3→from magneto import Magneto as Magneto_Lib
     4→from bdikit.download import get_cached_model_or_download
     5→from bdikit.schema_matching.base import ColumnMatch, BaseTopkSchemaMatcher
     6→
     7→DEFAULT_MAGNETO_MODEL = "magneto-gdc-v0.1"
     8→
     9→
    10→class MagnetoBase(BaseTopkSchemaMatcher):
    11→    def __init__(self, kwargs: Dict[str, Any] = None):
    12→        if kwargs is None:
    13→            kwargs = {}
    14→        self.magneto = Magneto_Lib(**kwargs)
    15→
    16→    def match_schema(
    17→        self, source: pd.DataFrame, target: pd.DataFrame
    18→    ) -> List[ColumnMatch]:
    19→        # Temporary workaround due to Magneto's top-1 matching issue
    20→        # Issue details: https://github.com/VIDA-NYU/magneto-matcher/issues/10
    21→        # Once resolved, this function will be removed to use the default implementation in the parent class.
    22→        matches = self.rank_schema_matches(
    23→            source, target, 2
    24→        )  # Get top-2 matches to avoid the issue
    25→
    26→        best_matches = {}
    27→        for match in matches:
    28→            if (
    29→                match.source_column not in best_matches
    30→                or match.similarity > best_matches[match.source_column].similarity
    31→            ):
    32→                best_matches[match.source_column] = match
    33→
    34→        matches = self._sort_matches(list(best_matches.values()))
    35→
    36→        return self._fill_missing_matches(source, matches)
    37→
    38→    def rank_schema_matches(
    39→        self, source: pd.DataFrame, target: pd.DataFrame, top_k: int
    40→    ) -> List[ColumnMatch]:
    41→        self.magneto.params["topk"] = (
    42→            top_k  # Magneto does not provide a method to set topk
    43→        )
    44→        raw_matches = self.magneto.get_matches(source, target)
    45→        target_columns = set(target.columns)
    46→        matches = []
    47→
    48→        for (source_column, target_column), score in raw_matches.items():
    49→            source_column = source_column[1]
    50→            target_column = target_column[1]
    51→            if target_column not in target_columns:
    52→                continue
    53→            matches.append(ColumnMatch(source_column, target_column, score))
    54→
    55→        matches = self._sort_ranked_matches(matches)
    56→
    57→        return self._fill_missing_matches(source, matches)
    58→

    61→    """Uses a zero-shot small language model as retriever with the bipartite algorithm as reranker in Magneto."""

    63→    def __init__(self):
    64→        super().__init__()

    99→    def __init__(
   100→        self,
   101→        encoding_mode: str = "header_values_verbose",
   102→        model_name: str = DEFAULT_MAGNETO_MODEL,
   103→        model_path: str = None,
   104→        reranker_model: str = "openai/gpt-4o-mini",
   105→        **reranker_kwargs

   107→        embedding_model = check_magneto_model(model_name, model_path)
   108→        if reranker_kwargs is None:
   109→            reranker_kwargs = {}
   110→
   111→        kwargs = {
   112→            "encoding_mode": encoding_mode,
   113→            "embedding_model": embedding_model,
   114→            "use_bp_reranker": False,
   115→            "use_gpt_reranker": True,
   116→            "llm_model": reranker_model,

1→"""
     2→Prompt composition logging for Harmonia.
     3→
     4→Two capabilities:
     5→1. print_prompt_composition() — prints full prompt layers to stdout for SLURM log inspection
     6→2. register_prompt_json_logger() — one-shot monkey-patch on agent.execute() that writes
     7→   structured JSON to the results directory on the first LLM call
     8→
     9→See documentation/plans/11_06_2025_1715_make_logging_full_prompt_in_container.md for design.
    10→"""
    11→
    12→import json
    13→import os
    14→import hashlib
    15→from datetime import datetime, timezone
    16→from pathlib import Path
    17→from typing import Optional
    18→
    19→
    20→# ============================================================
    21→# OUTPUT A: Stdout printing for visual inspection (sync)
    22→# ============================================================
    23→
    24→def print_prompt_composition(agent, context_slug: str) -> None:
    25→    """
    26→    Print the prompt layers available at init time to stdout.
    27→
    28→    Call this from Context.__init__() AFTER super().__init__() and all prompt
    29→    overrides (custom prelude, tool description overrides) have been applied.
    30→
    31→    This captures at init time:
    32→    - Layer 1: System message (ReAct prelude + model instructions + tool descriptions)
    33→    - Model-specific prompt instructions
    34→    - Custom prelude (if any)
    35→    - Prompt configuration env vars
    36→
    37→    The auto-context (domain prompt) is NOT available at init time because
    38→    auto_context()'s content_updater hasn't fired yet. That layer is printed
    39→    on first auto_context() call separately.
    40→
    41→    Args:
    42→        agent: The BeakerAgent/BDIKitAgent instance
    43→        context_slug: "bdikit_context" or "code_context"
    44→    """
    45→    separator = "=" * 80
    46→    subsep = "-" * 40
    47→
    48→    print(f"\n{separator}")
    49→    print(f"PROMPT COMPOSITION — {context_slug}")
    50→    print(f"Model class: {agent.model.__class__.__name__}")
    51→    print(f"Timestamp: {datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()}")
    52→    print(separator)
    53→
    54→    # Layer 1: System message (ReAct prelude + model instructions + tool descriptions)
    55→    system_msg = agent.chat_history.system_message
    56→    if system_msg:
    57→        content = system_msg.message.content if hasattr(system_msg, 'message') else str(system_msg)
    58→        print(f"\n{subsep}")
    59→        print("LAYER 1: SYSTEM MESSAGE (ReAct prelude + model instructions)")
    60→        print(subsep)
    61→        print(content)
    62→        print(f"[{len(content)} chars]")
    63→
    64→    # Model-specific prompt instructions
    65→    model_instructions = getattr(agent.model, 'MODEL_PROMPT_INSTRUCTIONS', '')
    66→    print(f"\n{subsep}")
    67→    print("MODEL-SPECIFIC PROMPT INSTRUCTIONS")
    68→    print(subsep)
    69→    if model_instructions.strip():
    70→        print(model_instructions)
    71→        print(f"[{len(model_instructions)} chars]")
    72→    else:
    73→        print("(none — empty for this model class)")
    74→
    75→    # Custom prelude
    76→    custom_prelude = getattr(agent, 'custom_prelude', None)
    77→    if custom_prelude:

   108→# ============================================================
   109→# OUTPUT B: Structured JSON logging for systematic comparison
   110→# ============================================================
   111→
   112→def _content_hash(text: str) -> str:
   113→    """SHA-256 hash of content for comparison across runs."""
   114→    return hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
   115→
   116→
   117→def build_prompt_composition_log(
   118→    messages: list,
   119→    model_class_name: str,
   120→    model_prompt_instructions: str,
   121→    custom_prelude: Optional[str],
   122→    experiment_name: str,
   123→    run_id: str,
   124→    context_slug: str,
   125→) -> dict:
   126→    """
   127→    Build a structured log of the full prompt composition.
   128→
   129→    Args:
   130→        messages: The full list of LangChain BaseMessage objects from ChatHistory.records()
   131→        model_class_name: e.g. "OllamaModel", "AnyLLMModel"
   132→        model_prompt_instructions: The MODEL_PROMPT_INSTRUCTIONS string
   133→        custom_prelude: The custom_prelude if set, else None
   134→        experiment_name: From experiment config
   135→        run_id: 8-char hex run ID
   136→        context_slug: "bdikit_context" or "code_context"
   137→
   138→    Returns:
   139→        Dict suitable for JSON serialization
   140→    """
   141→    # Collect prompt env vars for provenance
   142→    prompt_config = {
   143→        "HARMONIA_PROMPTS_DIR": os.environ.get("HARMONIA_PROMPTS_DIR"),
   144→        "HARMONIA_REACT_PRELUDE": os.environ.get("HARMONIA_REACT_PRELUDE"),
   145→        "HARMONIA_TOOL_PROMPTS_DIR": os.environ.get("HARMONIA_TOOL_PROMPTS_DIR"),
   146→        "HARMONIA_CODE_CONTEXT_PROMPT": os.environ.get("HARMONIA_CODE_CONTEXT_PROMPT"),
   147→    }
   148→
   149→    composition = {
   150→        "metadata": {
   151→            "timestamp": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
   152→            "run_id": run_id,
   153→            "experiment_name": experiment_name,
   154→            "context_type": context_slug,
   155→            "model_class": model_class_name,
   156→            "prompt_config": {k: v for k, v in prompt_config.items() if v is not None},
   157→        },
   158→        "layers": {},
   159→        "messages_sent_to_llm": [],
   160→        "summary": {},
   161→    }
   162→
   163→    # Decompose messages into layers
   164→    # Message order from ChatHistory.records():
   165→    #   0: system_message (SystemMessage)
   166→    #   1: auto_context_message (HumanMessage with domain prompt)
   167→    #   2+: summaries, user_preamble, raw_records
   168→
   169→    for i, msg in enumerate(messages):
   170→        content = msg.content if isinstance(msg.content, str) else str(msg.content)
   171→        msg_dict = {
   172→            "type": msg.__class__.__name__,
   173→            "content": content,
   174→            "index": i,
   175→            "content_hash": _content_hash(content),
   176→            "char_count": len(content),
   177→        }
   178→        composition["messages_sent_to_llm"].append(msg_dict)
   179→
   180→    # Identify layers by position and type
   181→    if messages:
   182→        system_content = messages[0].content if isinstance(messages[0].content, str) else str(messages[0].content)
   183→        composition["layers"]["system_message"] = {
   184→            "description": "ReAct prelude + model-specific instructions + tool descriptions",
   185→            "content": system_content,
   186→            "content_hash": _content_hash(system_content),
   187→            "char_count": len(system_content),
   188→            "custom_prelude_used": custom_prelude is not None,
   189→            "custom_prelude_hash": _content_hash(custom_prelude) if custom_prelude else None,
   190→        }
   191→
   192→    if len(messages) > 1:
   193→        auto_ctx_content = messages[1].content if isinstance(messages[1].content, str) else str(messages[1].content)
   194→        composition["layers"]["auto_context_message"] = {
   195→            "description": "Domain-specific system prompt (BDIKit harmonization or Code execution)",
   196→            "content": auto_ctx_content,
   197→            "content_hash": _content_hash(auto_ctx_content),
   198→            "char_count": len(auto_ctx_content),
   199→        }
   200→
   201→    # Model-specific instructions (embedded in system message but logged separately for comparison)
   202→    composition["layers"]["model_prompt_instructions"] = {
   203→        "description": "Model-class-specific prompt additions (e.g., OllamaModel tool message handling)",
   204→        "model_class": model_class_name,
   205→        "content": model_prompt_instructions,
   206→        "content_hash": _content_hash(model_prompt_instructions) if model_prompt_instructions else None,
   207→        "char_count": len(model_prompt_instructions),
   208→        "is_empty": len(model_prompt_instructions.strip()) == 0,
   209→    }
   210→
   211→    # Summary stats
   212→    total_chars = sum(len(m.content) if isinstance(m.content, str) else len(str(m.content)) for m in messages)
   213→    composition["summary"] = {
   214→        "total_messages": len(messages),
   215→        "total_char_count": total_chars,
   216→        "layer_count": len(composition["layers"]),
   217→        "has_custom_prelude": custom_prelude is not None,
   218→        "has_model_specific_instructions": len(model_prompt_instructions.strip()) > 0,
   219→        "uses_custom_prompts": any(v is not None for v in prompt_config.values()),
   220→    }
   221→
   222→    return composition
   223→
   224→
   225→def write_prompt_composition_log(
   226→    composition: dict,
   227→    results_dir: Path,
   228→) -> Path:
   229→    """
   230→    Write prompt composition log to results directory.
   231→
   232→    Args:
   233→        composition: Output of build_prompt_composition_log()
   234→        results_dir: Path to the experiment results directory
   235→
   236→    Returns:
   237→        Path to the written JSON file
   238→    """
   239→    output_path = results_dir / "full_prompt_composition.json"
   240→    output_path.write_text(json.dumps(composition, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
   241→    return output_path
   242→
   243→
   244→def register_prompt_json_logger(agent, context_slug: str) -> None:
   245→    """
   246→    Register a one-shot monkey-patch on Agent.execute() to capture
   247→    prompt composition as structured JSON on the first LLM call.
   248→
   249→    After firing once, it unwraps itself so subsequent calls are unaffected.
   250→
   251→    Reads results directory from RESULTS_DIR env var (set by exec_apptainer_harmonia.sh
   252→    to /workspace/results inside the container).
   253→
   254→    Args:
   255→        agent: The BeakerAgent/BDIKitAgent instance
   256→        context_slug: "bdikit_context" or "code_context"
   257→    """
   258→    results_dir_env = os.environ.get("RESULTS_DIR")
   259→    if not results_dir_env:
   260→        print("[Harmonia] RESULTS_DIR not set — skipping structured prompt JSON logging")
   261→        return
   262→
   263→    results_dir = Path(results_dir_env)
   264→    if not results_dir.exists():
   265→        print(f"[Harmonia] RESULTS_DIR={results_dir_env} does not exist — skipping JSON logging")
   266→        return
   267→
   268→    original_execute = agent.execute
   269→
   270→    async def logging_execute_wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
   271→        """One-shot wrapper: logs prompt composition, then unwraps."""
   272→        # Capture messages the same way execute() does
   273→        try:
   274→            records = await agent.chat_history.records(auto_update_context=True)
   275→            messages = [record.message for record in records]
   276→        except Exception as e:
   277→            print(f"[Harmonia] Warning: Could not capture messages for prompt log: {e}")
   278→            messages = []
   279→
   280→        if messages:
   281→            # Get model-specific info
   282→            model_class_name = agent.model.__class__.__name__
   283→            model_prompt_instructions = getattr(agent.model, 'MODEL_PROMPT_INSTRUCTIONS', '')
   284→            custom_prelude = getattr(agent, 'custom_prelude', None)
   285→
   286→            # Get run metadata from env vars
   287→            run_id = os.environ.get("HARMONIA_RUN_ID", "unknown")
   288→            experiment_name = os.environ.get("HARMONIA_EXPERIMENT_NAME", "unknown")
   289→
   290→            composition = build_prompt_composition_log(
   291→                messages=messages,
   292→                model_class_name=model_class_name,
   293→                model_prompt_instructions=model_prompt_instructions,
   294→                custom_prelude=custom_prelude,
   295→                experiment_name=experiment_name,
   296→                run_id=run_id,
   297→                context_slug=context_slug,
   298→            )
   299→
   300→            try:
   301→                output_path = write_prompt_composition_log(composition, results_dir)
   302→                print(f"[Harmonia] Structured prompt composition written to: {output_path}")
   303→            except Exception as e:
   304→                print(f"[Harmonia] Warning: Failed to write prompt composition: {e}")
   305→
   306→        # Unwrap — restore original execute for all subsequent calls
   307→        agent.execute = original_execute
   308→
   309→        # Call the real execute
   310→        return await original_execute(*args, **kwargs)
   311→
   312→    agent.execute = logging_execute_wrapper
   313→    print(f"[Harmonia] Registered one-shot prompt JSON logger (will fire on first LLM call)")
   314→

    58→
    59→        Uses HARMONIA_TOOL_PROMPTS_DIR env var for a custom tool prompts directory,

1→import json_repair
     2→import warnings
     3→from litellm import completion
     4→from typing import List, Dict, Any, Mapping
     5→from bdikit.value_matching.base import BaseValueMatcher, ValueMatch
     6→from bdikit.utils import get_additional_context
     7→from bdikit.config import VALUE_MATCHING_THRESHOLD
     8→
     9→
    10→class LLM(BaseValueMatcher):
    11→    """A value matcher that uses LLM to match values based on their similarity."""
    12→
    13→    def __init__(
    14→        self,
    15→        model_name: str = "openai/gpt-4o-mini",
    16→        threshold: float = VALUE_MATCHING_THRESHOLD,
    17→        **model_kwargs: Mapping[str, Any],
    18→    ):
    19→        self.model_name = model_name
    20→        self.threshold = threshold
    21→        self.model_kwargs = model_kwargs
    22→
    23→    def match_values(
    24→        self,
    25→        source_values: List[Any],
    26→        target_values: List[Any],
    27→        source_context: Dict[str, str] = None,
    28→        target_context: Dict[str, str] = None,
    29→    ) -> List[ValueMatch]:
    30→
    31→        if (
    32→            len(source_values) > 25
    33→        ):  # TODO: Improve this, avoid calling the API if the number of source values is too high (e.g. IDs)
    34→            return []
    35→        source_attribute = source_context["attribute_name"]
    36→        target_attribute = target_context["attribute_name"]
    37→        additional_source_cxt = get_additional_context(source_context, "source")
    38→        additional_target_cxt = get_additional_context(target_context, "target")
    39→        additional_context = additional_source_cxt + additional_target_cxt
    40→
    41→        target_values_set = set(target_values)
    42→        matches = []
    43→
    44→        for source_value in source_values:
    45→            response = completion(
    46→                model=self.model_name,
    47→                messages=[
    48→                    {
    49→                        "role": "system",
    50→                        "content": "You are an intelligent system that given a term, you have to choose a value from a list that best matches the term.",
    51→                    },
    52→                    {
    53→                        "role": "user",
    54→                        "content": f"For the term: '{source_value}', choose a value from this list {target_values}. "
    55→                        "Return the value from the list with a similarity score, between 0 and 1, with 1 indicating the highest similarity. "
    56→                        f"{additional_context}"
    57→                        "DO NOT PROVIDE ANY OTHER OUTPUT TEXT OR EXPLANATION. "
    58→                        'Only provide a Python dictionary. For example {"term": "term from the list", "score": 0.8}.',
    59→                    },
    60→                ],
    61→                **self.model_kwargs,
    62→            )
    63→
    64→            response_message = response.choices[0].message.content
    65→
    66→            try:
    67→                response_dict = json_repair.loads(response_message)
    68→                target_value = response_dict["term"]
    69→                score = float(response_dict["score"])
    70→                if target_value in target_values_set and score >= self.threshold:
    71→                    matches.append(
    72→                        ValueMatch(
    73→                            source_attribute,
    74→                            target_attribute,
    75→                            source_value,
    76→                            target_value,
    77→                            score,
    78→                        )
    79→                    )
    80→            except:
    81→                warnings.warn(
    82→                    f'Errors parsing response for "{source_value}": {response_message}',
    83→                    UserWarning,
    84→                )
    85→
    86→        matches = self._sort_matches(matches)
    87→
    88→        return self._fill_missing_matches(
    89→            source_values, matches, source_attribute, target_attribute
    90→        )
    91→

1→import re
     2→import random
     3→import textwrap
     4→import warnings
     5→import numpy as np
     6→from litellm import completion
     7→from typing import List, Dict, Any, Mapping
     8→from bdikit.utils import get_additional_context
     9→from bdikit.value_matching.base import BaseValueMatcher, ValueMatch
    10→
    11→
    12→random.seed(42)
    13→
    14→
    15→class LLMNumeric(BaseValueMatcher):
    16→    """A value matcher that uses LLM to derive formulas for numeric value matching."""
    17→
    18→    def __init__(
    19→        self,
    20→        model_name: str = "openai/gpt-4o-mini",
    21→        sample_size: int = 5,
    22→        **model_kwargs: Mapping[str, Any],
    23→    ):
    24→        self.model_name = model_name
    25→        self.sample_size = sample_size
    26→        self.model_kwargs = model_kwargs
    27→
    28→    def match_values(
    29→        self,
    30→        source_values: List[Any],
    31→        target_values: List[Any],
    32→        source_context: Dict[str, str] = None,
    33→        target_context: Dict[str, str] = None,
    34→    ) -> List[ValueMatch]:
    35→
    36→        matches = []
    37→        sample_values = []
    38→        source_attribute = source_context["attribute_name"]
    39→        target_attribute = target_context["attribute_name"]
    40→        additional_source_cxt = get_additional_context(source_context, "source")
    41→        additional_target_cxt = get_additional_context(target_context, "target")
    42→        additional_context = additional_source_cxt + additional_target_cxt
    43→
    44→        # For cases where source values are numeric but in string format, e.g. "1.0", "2.0"
    45→        clean_source_values = []
    46→        for source_value in source_values:
    47→            formatted_value = to_number(source_value)
    48→            if formatted_value is not None and len(sample_values) < self.sample_size:
    49→                sample_values.append(formatted_value)
    50→            clean_source_values.append(formatted_value)
    51→
    52→        response = completion(
    53→            model=self.model_name,
    54→            messages=[
    55→                {
    56→                    "role": "system",
    57→                    "content": "You are an intelligent system designed to derive formulas and write Python code "
    58→                    "to convert numeric source values into corresponding target values.",
    59→                },
    60→                {
    61→                    "role": "user",
    62→                    "content": "You are an intelligent system designed to derive formulas and write Python code "
    63→                    "to convert numeric source values into corresponding target values. "
    64→                    f"Given a dataset attribute named '{source_attribute}' containing the values: {str(sample_values)}, "
    65→                    f"and a potential target attribute named '{target_attribute}' described as: '{target_context['attribute_description']}'. "
    66→                    "Your task is to determine the formula needed to transform source values into target values. "
    67→                    f"{additional_context}"

    69→                    "Provide only the Python code snippet as a formatted string.",

    73→        )

    75→        function_code = response.choices[0].message.content

    87→
    88→        map_values_func = local_scope.get("map_values")
    89→
    90→        for index, clean_source_value in enumerate(clean_source_values):

   174→                [], target_values, source_attribute, target_attribute

    72→    vocabulary is supported.

   241→def match_values(
   242→    source: pd.DataFrame,
   243→    target: Union[str, pd.DataFrame],
   244→    attribute_matches: Union[Tuple[str, str], pd.DataFrame],
   245→    method: Optional[Union[str, BaseValueMatcher]] = DEFAULT_VALUE_MATCHING_METHOD,
   246→    source_context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
   247→    target_context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
   248→    method_args: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
   249→    standard_args: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
   250→    output_format: Optional[str] = "dataframe",
   251→    use_cache: Optional[bool] = True,
   252→) -> Union[pd.DataFrame, List[pd.DataFrame]]:
   253→    """
   254→    Finds matches between attribute values from the source dataset and attribute
   255→    values of the target domain (a pd.DataFrame or a standard dictionary such
   256→    as 'gdc') using the method provided in `method`.
   257→
   258→    Args:
   259→        source (pd.DataFrame): The source dataset containing the attributes/columns to be
   260→          matched.
   261→
   262→        target (Union[str, pd.DataFrame]): The target domain to match the
   263→          values to. It can be either a DataFrame or a standard vocabulary name.
   264→
   265→        attribute_matches (Union[Tuple[str, str], pd.DataFrame]): A tuple or a
   266→          DataFrame containing the mappings between source and target attributes.
   267→
   268→          - If a tuple is provided, it should contain two strings where the first
   269→            is the source attribute and the second is the target attribute.
   270→          - If a DataFrame is provided, it should contain 'source_attribute' and 'target_attribute'
   271→            column names where each row specifies a attribute mapping.
   272→
   273→        method (str, optional): The name of the method to use for value
   274→          matching.
   275→        source_context (Dict[str, Any], optional): The context for the source
   276→            dataset, which can include additional information, such as descriptions or metadata.
   277→        target_context (Dict[str, Any], optional): The context for the target
   278→            dataset, which can include additional information, such as descriptions or metadata.
   279→        method_args (Dict[str, Any], optional): The additional arguments of the
   280→            method for value matching.
   281→        standard_args (Dict[str, Any], optional): The additional arguments of the
   282→            standard vocabulary.
   283→        output_format (str, optional): The format of the output. If "dataframe",
   284→            a single DataFrame is returned. If "list", a list of DataFrames is returned.
   285→            Defaults to "dataframe".
   286→        use_cache (bool, optional): Whether to use caching for the value matching results.
   287→            Defaults to True.
   288→
   289→    Returns:
   290→        pd.DataFrame: A DataFrame or a List of DataFrames containing the results of value matching
   291→        between the source and target values.
   292→    Raises:
   293→        ValueError: If the attribute_matches DataFrame does not contain 'source_attribute' and
   294→          'target_attribute' columns.
   295→        ValueError: If the target is neither a DataFrame nor a standard vocabulary name.
   296→        ValueError: If the source attribute is not present in the source dataset.
   297→    """
   298→
   299→    source_dataset = _load_dataset(source)
   300→    target_dataset = _load_dataset(target, standard_args)
   301→    matcher_instance = _load_value_matcher(method, method_args)
   302→
   303→    all_matches: List[ValueMatch] = []
   304→
   305→    for (
   306→        source_attribute,
   307→        target_attribute,
   308→        source_values,
   309→        target_values,
   310→    ) in _iterate_values(source_dataset, target_dataset, attribute_matches):
   311→        source_ctx = _create_context(
   312→            source_dataset,
   313→            source_attribute,
   314→            user_context=source_context,
   315→        )
   316→        target_ctx = _create_context(
   317→            target_dataset,
   318→            target_attribute,
   319→            user_context=target_context,
   320→        )
   321→
   322→        if use_cache:
   323→            matches = _cache_value_matches(
   324→                source_values=source_values,
   325→                target_values=target_values,
   326→                source_ctx=source_ctx,
   327→                target_ctx=target_ctx,
   328→                match_func=matcher_instance.match_values,
   329→                matcher_obj=matcher_instance,
   330→            )
   331→        else:
   332→            matches = matcher_instance.match_values(
   333→                source_values, target_values, source_ctx, target_ctx
   334→            )
   335→        all_matches.extend(matches)
   336→
   337→    matches = BaseValueMatcher.sort_multiple_matches(all_matches)
   338→
   339→    matches = pd.DataFrame(
   340→        data=matches,
   341→        columns=[
   342→            "source_attribute",
   343→            "target_attribute",
   344→            "source_value",
   345→            "target_value",
   346→            "similarity",
   347→        ],
   348→    )
   349→
   350→    if output_format == "dataframe":
   351→        return matches
   352→    elif output_format == "list":
   353→        return _convert_to_list_of_dataframes(matches)
   354→    else:
   355→        raise ValueError(
   356→            "The output_format must be either 'dataframe' or 'list'. "
   357→            f"Received: {output_format}"
   358→        )

   572→def view_value_matches(

   574→):
   575→    """
   576→    Shows the value match results grouped by source and target attributes matches
   577→
   578→    Args:

   580→        match_values() or rank_value_matches().
   581→
   582→        edit (bool, optional): Whether or not to edit the values within the DataFrame. Editable mode works only in Jupyter notebooks.
   583→    """
   584→
   585→    def regular_display():
   586→        if isinstance(matches, pd.DataFrame):
   587→            print(matches)
   588→        else:
   589→            for match_df in matches:
   590→                print(match_df)
   591→
   592→    # Check if we are in a Jupyter notebook environment
   593→    try:
   594→        from IPython.display import display, HTML
   595→        from IPython import get_ipython
   596→
   597→        shell = get_ipython().__class__.__name__
   598→        if shell != "ZMQInteractiveShell":
   599→            regular_display()
   600→            return
   601→    except ImportError:
   602→        regular_display()
   603→        return
   604→
   605→    if isinstance(matches, list):
   606→        # Grouping DataFrames by metadata (source_attribute and target_attribute columns)
   607→        grouped_matches = defaultdict(list)
   608→        for match_df in matches:
   609→            grouped_matches[
   610→                match_df.attrs["source_attribute"], match_df.attrs["target_attribute"]
   611→            ].append(match_df)
   612→
   613→        # Display grouped DataFrames
   614→        for (source_col, target_col), match_dfs in grouped_matches.items():
   615→            display(
   616→                HTML(

   628→    elif isinstance(matches, pd.DataFrame):
   629→        # Create a grouped dictionary to hold widgets for each group
   630→        grouped = matches.groupby(["source_attribute", "target_attribute"], sort=False)
   631→        tabulators = {}
   632→
   633→        # Function to synchronize changes back to the original dataframe
   634→        def sync_changes(event):
   635→            for (source_attr, target_attr), tabulator in tabulators.items():
   636→                updated_sub_df = tabulator.value
   637→                # Update the relevant part of the original dataframe
   638→                mask = (matches["source_attribute"] == source_attr) & (
   639→                    matches["target_attribute"] == target_attr
   640→                )
   641→                matches.loc[mask, ["source_value", "target_value", "similarity"]] = (

   644→                    ].values
   645→                )
   646→
   647→        for (source_attr, target_attr), group in grouped:
   648→            sub_df = group[["source_value", "target_value", "similarity"]].reset_index(

   651→            display(

   654→                    f"<strong>Target attribute:</strong> {target_attr}"
   655→                )
   656→            )
   657→            if edit:
   658→                tabulator = pn.widgets.Tabulator(
   659→                    sub_df,
   660→                    disabled=not edit,
   661→                )
   662→                # Attach sync callback to updates
   663→                tabulator.param.watch(sync_changes, "value")
   664→                tabulators[(source_attr, target_attr)] = tabulator
   665→                display(tabulator)
   666→
   667→            else:
   668→                display(sub_df)
   669→    else:
   670→        raise ValueError(
   671→            "The matches must be either a DataFrame or a list of DataFrames."

   675→def preview_domain(
   676→    dataset: Union[str, pd.DataFrame],
   677→    attribute: str,
   678→    limit: Optional[int] = None,
   679→    standard_args: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
   680→) -> pd.DataFrame:
   681→    """
   682→    Preview the domain, i.e. set of unique values, attribute description and value description
   683→    (if applicable) of the given attribute of the source or target dataset.
   684→
   685→    Args:
   686→        dataset (Union[str, pd.DataFrame], optional): The dataset or standard vocabulary name
   687→        containing the attribute to preview.
   688→            If a string is provided and it is equal to "gdc", the domain will be retrieved
   689→            from the GDC data.
   690→            If a DataFrame is provided, the domain will be retrieved from the specified DataFrame.
   691→        attribute(str): The attribute name to show the domain.
   692→        limit (int, optional): The maximum number of unique values to include in the preview.
   693→            Defaults to None.
   694→        standard_args (Dict[str, Any], optional): The additional arguments of the standard vocabulary.
   695→
   696→    Returns:
   697→        pd.DataFrame: A DataFrame containing the unique domain values (or a sample of
   698→        them if the parameter `limit` was specified), attribute description and value description
   699→        (if applicable).
   700→    """
   701→
   702→    if isinstance(dataset, str):
   703→        if standard_args is None:
   704→            standard_args = {}
   705→        standard = Standards.get_standard(dataset, **standard_args)
   706→        attribute_metadata = standard.get_attribute_metadata([attribute])
   707→        value_names = attribute_metadata[attribute]["value_names"]
   708→        value_descriptions = attribute_metadata[attribute]["value_descriptions"]
   709→        attribute_description = attribute_metadata[attribute]["description"]
   710→        assert len(value_names) == len(value_descriptions)
   711→    elif isinstance(dataset, pd.DataFrame):
   712→        value_names = dataset[attribute].unique()
   713→        value_descriptions = []
   714→        attribute_description = ""
   715→    else:
   716→        raise ValueError(
   717→            "The dataset must be a DataFrame or a standard vocabulary name."
   718→        )
   719→
   720→    if isinstance(limit, int):
   721→        value_names = value_names[:limit]
   722→        value_descriptions = value_descriptions[:limit]
   723→
   724→    domain = {}
   725→
   726→    if len(value_names) > 0:
   727→        domain["value_name"] = value_names
   728→
   729→    if len(value_descriptions) > 0:
   730→        domain["value_description"] = value_descriptions
   731→
   732→    if len(attribute_description) > 0:
   733→        empty_rows_size = len(value_names) - 1
   734→        domain["attribute_description"] = [attribute_description] + [
   735→            ""
   736→        ] * empty_rows_size
   737→
   738→    return pd.DataFrame(domain)
   739→

   741→def evaluate_schema_matches(
   742→    source: pd.DataFrame,
   743→    target: Union[str, pd.DataFrame],
   744→    schema_matches: pd.DataFrame,
   745→    standard_args: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
   746→) -> pd.DataFrame:
   747→    """
   748→    Evaluates the schema matches by providing a response and an explanation for each match.
   749→
   750→    Args:
   751→        source (pd.DataFrame): The source dataset.
   752→        target (Union[str, pd.DataFrame]): The target dataset or standard vocabulary name.
   753→        schema_matches (pd.DataFrame): The DataFrame containing the schema matches with columns
   754→            'source_attribute', 'target_attribute', and 'similarity'.
   755→        standard_args (Dict[str, Any], optional): Additional arguments for the standard vocabulary.
   756→
   757→    Returns:
   758→        pd.DataFrame: A DataFrame containing the evaluated matches with additional columns
   759→        'response' and 'explanation'.
   760→    """
   761→    evaluated_matches = schema_matches.copy()
   762→
   763→    evaluated_matches["response"], evaluated_matches["explanation"] = zip(
   764→        *evaluated_matches.apply(
   765→            lambda row: evaluate_schema_match(
   766→                {
   767→                    "source_column": row["source_attribute"],
   768→                    "target_column": row["target_attribute"],
   769→                    "similarity": row["similarity"],
   770→                    "source_domain": preview_domain(source, row["source_attribute"]),
   771→                    "target_domain": preview_domain(
   772→                        target, row["target_attribute"], standard_args=standard_args
   773→                    ),
   774→                }
   775→            ),
   776→            axis=1,
   777→        )
   778→    )
   779→
   780→    return evaluated_matches

   783→def evaluate_value_matches(
   784→    source: pd.DataFrame,

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# Build Script for Harmonia Beaker LLM Agent Environment Apptainer Image
# =============================================================================
#
# This script builds the harmonia_beaker_LLM_agent_environment_apptainer.sif
# container image with full any-llm-sdk support for unified LLM provider access.
#
# Usage:
#   # Interactive build (recommended for first time/debugging)
#   srun -J apptainer_build_claude-code --time=02:00:00 --mem=32G --gres=tmpspace:100G bash
#   ./build_harmonia_apptainer.sh
#
#   # Or submit as batch job
#   sbatch --job-name=apptainer_build --time=02:00:00 --mem=32G --gres=tmpspace:100G ./build_harmonia_apptainer.sh
#
# =============================================================================

set -e

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
cd "$SCRIPT_DIR"

# Configuration
DEF_FILE="harmonia_beaker_LLM_agent_environment_apptainer.def"
SIF_FILE="harmonia_beaker_LLM_agent_environment_apptainer.sif"

echo "=============================================="
echo "Harmonia Apptainer Build Script"
echo "=============================================="
echo ""

# ============================================
# Phase 1: Environment Diagnostics
# ============================================
echo "========== PHASE 1: ENVIRONMENT =========="
echo "Date: $(date)"
echo "TMPDIR: $TMPDIR"
echo "SLURM_JOB_ID: $SLURM_JOB_ID"
echo "HOME: $HOME"
echo "PWD: $(pwd)"
echo "DEF_FILE: $DEF_FILE"
echo "SIF_FILE: $SIF_FILE"
echo ""

if [ -z "$TMPDIR" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: TMPDIR is not set! Run this inside an srun allocation."
    echo ""
    echo "Example:"
    echo "  srun -J apptainer_build_claude-code --time=02:00:00 --mem=32G --gres=tmpspace:100G bash"
    echo "  ./build_harmonia_apptainer.sh"
    exit 1
fi

# Verify def file exists
if [ ! -f "$DEF_FILE" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: Definition file not found: $DEF_FILE"
    exit 1
fi

# ============================================
# Phase 2: Space Diagnostics
# ============================================
echo "========== PHASE 2: SPACE CHECK =========="

echo "--- Scratch space ($TMPDIR) ---"
df -h $TMPDIR
AVAILABLE_GB=$(df -BG $TMPDIR | tail -1 | awk '{print $4}' | sed 's/G//')
echo "Available: ${AVAILABLE_GB}GB"
echo ""

# Recommend at least 50GB for the build
REQUIRED_GB=50
if [ "$AVAILABLE_GB" -lt "$REQUIRED_GB" ]; then
    echo "WARNING: Low disk space!"
    echo "   You have ${AVAILABLE_GB}GB but recommend ~${REQUIRED_GB}GB"
    echo "   Request more with: --gres=tmpspace:${REQUIRED_GB}G"
    echo ""
    read -p "Continue anyway? (y/N) " -n 1 -r
    echo
    if [[ ! $REPLY =~ ^[Yy]$ ]]; then
        echo "Aborting."
        exit 1
    fi
else
    echo "Sufficient space available"
fi
echo ""

# ============================================
# Phase 3: Setup Build Environment
# ============================================
echo "========== PHASE 3: SETUP =========="

export APPTAINER_TMPDIR=$TMPDIR
export APPTAINER_CACHEDIR=$TMPDIR

SANDBOX_DIR=$TMPDIR/sandbox_harmonia
BUILD_TMP=$TMPDIR/build_tmp_harmonia

echo "APPTAINER_TMPDIR: $APPTAINER_TMPDIR"
echo "APPTAINER_CACHEDIR: $APPTAINER_CACHEDIR"
echo "SANDBOX_DIR: $SANDBOX_DIR"
echo "BUILD_TMP: $BUILD_TMP"
echo ""

# Clean up previous attempts
echo "Cleaning previous builds..."
rm -rf $SANDBOX_DIR
rm -rf $BUILD_TMP

# Backup existing sif if present
if [ -f "$SIF_FILE" ]; then
    BACKUP_FILE="${SIF_FILE}.backup.$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)"
    echo "Backing up existing $SIF_FILE to $BACKUP_FILE"
    mv "$SIF_FILE" "$BACKUP_FILE"
fi

# Create build temp directory
mkdir -p $BUILD_TMP
echo "Created $BUILD_TMP"

# Check space after cleanup
echo ""
echo "Space after cleanup:"
df -h $TMPDIR
echo ""

# ============================================
# Phase 4: Build Sandbox
# ============================================
echo "========== PHASE 4: BUILDING SANDBOX =========="
echo "Using --bind to mount scratch as container's /tmp"
echo "Command: apptainer build --sandbox --bind $BUILD_TMP:/tmp $SANDBOX_DIR $DEF_FILE"
echo ""

# Monitor space usage during build in background
(
    while true; do
        sleep 60
        echo "[SPACE MONITOR] $(date +%H:%M:%S) - Scratch: $(df -h $TMPDIR | tail -1 | awk '{print $4}') free"
    done
) &
MONITOR_PID=$!

# Trap to kill monitor on exit
trap "kill $MONITOR_PID 2>/dev/null" EXIT

# Build the sandbox
apptainer build --sandbox --bind $BUILD_TMP:/tmp $SANDBOX_DIR $DEF_FILE

# Stop the monitor
kill $MONITOR_PID 2>/dev/null || true

# ============================================
# Phase 5: Verify Sandbox
# ============================================
echo "========== PHASE 5: VERIFY SANDBOX =========="

if [ -f "$SANDBOX_DIR/bin/sh" ]; then
    echo "Shell exists"
else
    echo "ERROR: /bin/sh missing!"
    ls -la $SANDBOX_DIR/ 2>/dev/null || echo "Sandbox directory doesn't exist"
    exit 1
fi

if [ -f "$REDACTED" ]; then
    echo "Python exists"
else
    echo "WARNING: Python not at expected location"
fi

echo ""
echo "Sandbox size:"
du -sh $SANDBOX_DIR
echo ""

echo "Testing key imports in sandbox..."
apptainer exec $SANDBOX_DIR python3 -c "from bdikit_context.llm.anyllm import AnyLLMModel; print('AnyLLMModel: OK')" || echo "FAILED: AnyLLMModel import"
apptainer exec $SANDBOX_DIR python3 -c "from any_llm import AnyLLM; print('AnyLLM: OK')" || echo "FAILED: AnyLLM import"
apptainer exec $SANDBOX_DIR python3 -c "from bdikit_context.context import BDIKitContext; print('BDIKitContext: OK')" || echo "FAILED: BDIKitContext import"
echo ""

# ============================================
# Phase 6: Convert to SIF
# ============================================
echo "========== PHASE 6: CONVERT TO SIF =========="
apptainer build $SIF_FILE $SANDBOX_DIR

# ============================================
# Phase 7: Final Verification
# ============================================
echo "========== PHASE 7: FINAL VERIFICATION =========="
echo "Testing SIF image..."

apptainer exec $SIF_FILE /bin/sh -c "echo 'Shell works'"
apptainer exec $SIF_FILE python --version && echo "Python works"
apptainer exec $SIF_FILE python -c "from bdikit_context.llm.anyllm import AnyLLMModel; print('AnyLLMModel import: OK')"
apptainer exec $SIF_FILE python -c "from any_llm import AnyLLM; print('AnyLLM import: OK')"

echo ""
echo "Final image size:"
ls -lh $SIF_FILE

# ============================================
# Phase 8: Cleanup
# ============================================
echo "========== PHASE 8: CLEANUP =========="
rm -rf $SANDBOX_DIR
rm -rf $BUILD_TMP
echo "Cleaned up temporary directories"

echo ""
echo "=============================================="
echo "BUILD COMPLETE"
echo "=============================================="
echo ""
echo "Image: $SIF_FILE"
echo "Size: $(ls -lh $SIF_FILE | awk '{print $5}')"
echo ""
echo "To use:"
echo "  ./exec_apptainer_harmonia.sh --config configs/manual/dou_harmonization_manual_devstral-small.yaml"

        self,
        dataset: str,
        agent: AgentRef,
        target: Optional[str] = None,
        method: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> str:
        """
        This function performs schema mapping between the source table and the given target schema.
        The target is either a DataFrame or a string representing a standard data vocabulary supported by the library.
        Currently, only the GDC (Genomic Data Commons) standard vocabulary is supported.

        Args:
            dataset (str): The name of the dataset variable.
            target (str, optional): The target table or standard data vocabulary.
            method (str, optional): The method used for mapping.

        Returns:
            str: returns the matched columns

        You should show the user the result after this function runs.
        """

        if target is None or target == "":
            target = DEFAULT_TARGET
        if method is None or method == "":
            method = DEFAULT_SCHEMA_METHOD

        # Validate target
        if target not in VALID_TARGETS:
            return f"Error: Invalid target '{target}'. Valid targets are: {', '.join(VALID_TARGETS)}. Please try again with a valid target."

        # Validate method
        if method not in VALID_SCHEMA_METHODS:
            return f"Error: Invalid method '{method}'. Valid methods are: {', '.join(VALID_SCHEMA_METHODS)}. Please try again with a valid method."

        code = agent.context.get_code(
            "match_schema",
            {
                "dataset": dataset,
                "target": target,
                "method": method,
            },
        )
        result = await agent.context.evaluate(
            code,
            parent_header={},
        )

        match_result = result.get("return")

        return match_result

        also the `source` and `target` columns as DataFrame attributes. The DataFrames created

    def _override_tool_descriptions(self):
